plan: In a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ strategies. Overbidding risks paying more than your value; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. There’s only 1 round and no history to exploit, so no strategic shading or signaling is beneficial. With a value of $8, bid exactly 8 to secure any win priced below or equal to your value while paying the second-highest bid.

[ This is a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values. Truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: it wins exactly when my value exceeds others’ highest bid and I pay that second-highest bid. Underbidding can forgo positive-profit wins; overbidding can cause negative-profit wins if I beat a higher opponent and pay above my value. There’s no history to exploit and values are redrawn, so no dynamic adjustment. My value is 42; $0.1 increments permit 42.0. I will bid my value to maximize expected profit. ]

[ In a 3-bidder sealed-bid second-price auction with i.i.d. uniform private values, truthful bidding is a dominant strategy. Bidding my exact value maximizes expected profit: shading risks losing when I should win and doesn’t reduce the second price when I do win. With value 13, I bid 13.0. There’s no history to adjust to in round 1. Tie risk with 0.1 increments is minimal. ]
